artist_statement.text:
**the Artist in teh Open Sea**

A man rows a bathtub through lanes of rush-hour traffic. The slowest participant in the frame, he’s the only one going anywhere of his own. There is no water here. The sea he was promised turned out to be traffic. The road is infrastructure built for speed and volume, there is no place in it for anyone moving at their own pace. Still he rows, unhurried, as if the promise were worth holding to even after the water is gone. What he holds is little, but all of it is his.

This is the artist in the marketplace: present, visible, but structurally ignored, moving by muscle through a system that moves by volume. Platforms that call themselves open seas are in fact corridors, permissioned for velocity and trade, with no lane for meaningful creation, no attention to  what the small fish needs. There is no application for what the artist is doing, however that is the point: the free act is the one that never asks.

6000 x 4000 px composite long exposure digital photograph. Directed, shot on Canon 6DMII, edited and color graded by Hugo Faz.

I, Hugo Faz, hereby confirm that I hold full rights over the submitted work and formally consent for this work to be released under CC0, relinquishing all copyright and related rights, and permanently accessioned as part of the 6529 Network Museum collection.

Shot on July 6th, 2026, in São Paulo, Brazil, and submitted to Keys and gates on the same date.
